free_tier.stated: Free: 15 players, $0/mo, 1 network, 1 backend, Strict L4/L7 DDoS mitigation, Real client IPs (PROXY protocol)

egress.terms: Bandwidth to backend per month: Fair use on Free, Unlimited on Budget and above. No byte figure is given for fair use.; ingress: tcp

interface_detail: Self-serve panel at beta-panel.arvoris.net; setup is a single DNS record on every plan.
chaining: DNS in front of a public origin, so it hides an address but does not create one.
binding_note: No byte number is published for the free plan's fair-use allowance, and no UDP port is offered anywhere on the page, so nothing can reach a 1 TiB/month quota here.

identity_cost.detail: 'free plan, no card required'; an account at beta-panel.arvoris.net/register. The register form was not opened, so its fields are unread.

reliability_note: Free tier is capped at 15 players and community support; the fair-use bandwidth term has no published threshold.
confidence_note: The plan table and FAQ are first-party and were read in full. The negative on UDP comes from the landing page and the plan comparison table only, and an absence is weaker than a statement; docs.arvoris.net would settle whether a Bedrock path exists.

evidence.proved: Free plan at $0/mo: 15 players, 1 network, 1 backend, strict L4/L7, real client IPs, 24-hour analytics; no card required
Bandwidth to backend per month is 'Fair use' on Free and 'Unlimited' from Budget up; every tier routes by DNS record and speaks Minecraft hostnames
The stack is described as Cloudflare Spectrum powered with a hostname-aware L7 engine, which is a TCP-with-SNI shape rather than a per-customer UDP IP

notes: Budget brand of papyrus.vip, Cloudflare Spectrum backed. Everything read describes hostname-routed Minecraft Java; no Bedrock or generic UDP line item appears on the landing page or in the four-tier comparison table. Recorded as fails-egress rather than dead: the service is alive, it just has no UDP product in what.

extras.wg_detail: No WireGuard offering and no UDP port on any tier.
